items.title: feat(rules): add MCP009 rule to detect hardcoded API keys and secrets in tool handlers
items.summary: Detect hardcoded credentials (e.g., `sk-...`, `ghp_...`, `AKIA...`, `Bearer ...`, or assignments to `api_key` / `secret` string literals) inside `@mcp.tool()` functions.
items.motivation: Developers prototyping MCP servers frequently paste API keys directly into tool modules before publishing. Catching high-confidence secret patterns in `vexar-mcp scan` prevents accidental credential leaks.
acceptance_criteria: Scan string constants inside decorated tool functions for common token prefixes (`ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `sk-`, `AKIA`, `xoxb-`) and sensitive variable assignments.
Register rule `MCP009` (`hardcoded-secret-in-tool`, severity `ERROR`, category `SECURITY`) via `@register_rule`.
Ignore placeholder strings such as `YOUR_API_KEY`, `example`, `<token>`, or empty strings (`os.environ[...]`).
Add unit tests covering both positive detections and placeholder/env-var non-triggers.

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP010 rule flagging outbound HTTP calls missing explicit `timeout=`
items.summary: Flag `requests.get/post/...`, `httpx.get/post/...`, and `urllib.request.urlopen(...)` calls inside MCP tools when no `timeout` keyword argument is provided.
items.motivation: An MCP tool that hangs indefinitely on a stalled upstream socket blocks the entire LLM agent turn and stdio transport pipe.
acceptance_criteria: Record outbound HTTP call AST nodes that omit `timeout=...` (or pass `timeout=None`).
Register rule `MCP010` (`missing-network-timeout`, severity `WARNING`, category `SECURITY`).
Ensure `examples/clean_server.py` continues to score `100/100 (A+)` (it already passes `timeout=5`).
Add unit tests for `requests.get(url)` (flagged) vs `requests.get(url, timeout=10)` (clean).

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP011 rule for SQL string interpolation in `.execute(...)` calls
items.summary: Detect f-strings, `%` formatting, `.format(...)`, or `+` string concatenation inside `cursor.execute(...)` / `session.execute(...)` when referencing tool parameters.
items.motivation: Database MCP servers are one of the most common MCP server types, and LLM-generated arguments can trivially trigger SQL injection if interpolated directly into SQL strings.
acceptance_criteria: Detect `.execute(...)` / `.executemany(...)` calls whose first argument is an `ast.JoinedStr` (f-string), `ast.BinOp` (`%` or `+`), or `.format()` call referencing a tool parameter.
Register `MCP011` (`sql-string-interpolation`, severity `ERROR`, category `SECURITY`).
Allow parameterized queries (`cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', (user_id,))`) without false positives.
Add unit tests for f-string SQL vs parameterized SQL.

items.title: feat(reporters): add `--format github` reporter for inline GitHub Actions PR annotations
items.summary: Add a `--format github` output option to `vexar-mcp scan` that emits GitHub Actions workflow commands (`::error`, `::warning`, `::notice`).
items.motivation: Emitting `::error file=server.py,line=24,title=MCP005 (dangerous-shell-execution)::...` lets GitHub render inline annotations directly on changed lines in Pull Request diffs without requiring GitHub Advanced Security / SARIF upload.
acceptance_criteria: Implement `render_github_annotations(report: ScanReport) -> str` mapping `ERROR -> ::error`, `WARNING -> ::warning`, `INFO -> ::notice`.
Properly escape `%`, `\r`, and `\n` in workflow command messages per GitHub Actions spec.
Wire `--format github` into `vexar-mcp scan` CLI choices.
Add CLI tests verifying exact annotation lines.

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP015 rule when tool parameters have no description
items.summary: Flag tool parameters that carry no description, so an agent cannot infer when to supply them. MCP001 covers the tool description; parameter-level docs are unchecked.
items.motivation: Rule IDs are a public contract and MCP012 now means live protocol/transport validation. This item originally requested MCP012, then MCP014, and both were claimed by other rules -- so the next available ID is MCP015. Check `vexar-mcp rules` before claiming an ID.
acceptance_criteria: Register rule `MCP015` (severity `INFO`, category `SCHEMA`) via `@register_rule`.
Emit at most one finding per tool, listing the undocumented parameters.
Do not fire when the tool has fewer than two parameters.
Document the rule in `README.md` and `docs/rules.md`, and add tests for both loaders.

items.title: feat(parsers): add TypeScript MCP SDK (`server.tool(...)`) static loader
items.summary: Support scanning `.ts` and `.js` MCP servers built with `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` (`server.tool(name, description, zodSchema, handler)` and `registerTool(...)`).
items.motivation: Roughly half of public MCP servers are written in TypeScript. Supporting `.ts`/`.js` files without requiring a Node runtime makes `vexar-mcp` a universal cross-language MCP auditor.
acceptance_criteria: Extract tool name, description, basic Zod parameter names/types (`z.string()`, `z.number().max(...)`, `z.any()`), and dangerous sinks (`child_process.exec`, `eval`) from `.ts`/`.js` files.
Register `.ts` and `.js` extensions in `discover_candidate_files` and `scan_paths`.
Ignore `*.d.ts` declaration files and `node_modules`.
Add fixture-based tests covering clean and vulnerable TypeScript MCP servers.

items.title: feat(cli): add `vexar-mcp init` command to scaffold `vexar-mcp.toml` and CI workflow
items.summary: Add an `vexar-mcp init [--github-action]` subcommand that generates a commented `vexar-mcp.toml` config file and optional `.github/workflows/mcp-doctor.yml`.
items.motivation: One-command onboarding drastically lowers friction for maintainers adopting `vexar-mcp` in existing MCP server repositories.
acceptance_criteria: Create `vexar-mcp.toml` with documented defaults (`max-tool-tokens`, `max-server-tokens`, `ignore`, `exclude`).
Refuse to overwrite existing files unless `--force` is passed.
When `--github-action` is passed, write `.github/workflows/vexar-mcp.yml` referencing `RANJITHROSAN17/Vexar-MCP@main`.
Add unit tests covering fresh creation, existing-file protection, and `--force`.

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP013 rule for unsafe deserialization (`pickle.loads`, `yaml.load`)
items.summary: Detect `pickle.loads`, `pickle.load`, `marshal.loads`, `shelve.open`, and `yaml.load` (without `SafeLoader`) inside MCP tool functions.
items.motivation: Deserializing untrusted payloads inside an MCP tool leads directly to arbitrary code execution.
acceptance_criteria: Detect unsafe deserialization calls in `python_ast.py`, treating `yaml.safe_load(...)` and `yaml.load(..., Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)` as safe.
Register `MCP013` (`unsafe-deserialization`, severity `ERROR`, category `SECURITY`).
Add unit tests verifying `yaml.load(data)` triggers `MCP013` while `yaml.safe_load(data)` passes.

items.title: feat(parsers): expand Pydantic `BaseModel` and `TypedDict` parameter schemas
items.summary: Resolve in-file `BaseModel` and `TypedDict` classes referenced by `@mcp.tool()` parameters so nested fields are audited for types, bounds, and token footprint.
items.motivation: Many FastMCP servers group tool arguments into a Pydantic `BaseModel` (`def search(req: SearchRequest)`). Expanding its fields unlocks accurate `MCP002`/`MCP003`/`MCP004` diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Index class definitions inheriting from `BaseModel` or `TypedDict` in the same module.
Expand their annotated attributes (including `Field(le=..., max_length=..., description=...)`) into `ParameterSpec` entries.
Update token estimation accordingly and add unit tests.

items.title: feat(cli): add `vexar-mcp audit-server -- <cmd>` live MCP server introspection
items.summary: Spawn any MCP server command over JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio, perform handshake + `tools/list`, and run all schema/contract/token rules on the live advertised tools.
items.motivation: Dynamic MCP servers (written in Go, Rust, Java, or dynamically registered in Python) can be audited at runtime via standard MCP `tools/list` JSON-RPC without needing language-specific AST parsers.
acceptance_criteria: Implement minimal stdlib `subprocess` JSON-RPC 2.0 `initialize` -> `notifications/initialized` -> `tools/list` client with configurable timeout.
Feed returned `tools` array through existing `json_manifest` normalizer and scan engine.
Test against a tiny mock stdio Python script in `tests/`.

items.title: feat(reporters): add standalone interactive HTML report (`--format html`)
items.summary: Generate a zero-external-asset HTML dashboard (`--format html`) displaying the health grade, per-tool token usage bars, and filterable diagnostics.
items.motivation: Teams running `vexar-mcp` in CI artifacts want a single shareable HTML report with zero CDN dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: Emit valid self-contained HTML5 with inline CSS and escaped diagnostic strings (`html.escape`).
Include health score badge, per-tool token breakdown table, and severity filter toggles.
Add unit tests verifying HTML escaping and CLI `--format html` execution.

items.title: feat(cli): add `--baseline <path>` to suppress pre-existing findings
items.summary: Allow generating and passing a baseline JSON snapshot so CI only fails on newly introduced findings.
items.motivation: Large existing MCP servers (50+ tools) need a way to turn on `vexar-mcp` in CI immediately without fixing every historical warning on day one.
acceptance_criteria: Support `--write-baseline .mcp-doctor-baseline.json` and `--baseline .mcp-doctor-baseline.json`.
Match baseline entries by `(rule_id, tool_name, source_file)` fingerprint rather than brittle line numbers.
Add CLI tests demonstrating existing findings suppressed while new findings fail.

items.title: feat(rules): add server-wide token budget warning (`MCP014`) when total context tax exceeds `max-server-tokens`
items.summary: Emit `MCP014` (`excessive-server-tokens`) when the sum of all discovered tools' estimated tokens exceeds `ScanConfig.max_server_tokens` (default `4000`).
items.motivation: Even if each individual tool stays at 200 tokens, exposing 35 tools on a single MCP server silently burns 7,000+ tokens on every conversation turn.
acceptance_criteria: Register `MCP014` (`excessive-server-tokens`, severity `WARNING`, category `TOKENS`).
Trigger once when `sum(t.estimated_tokens for t in tools) > config.max_server_tokens`, naming the top 3 heaviest tools in the message.
Add unit tests with custom `ScanConfig(max_server_tokens=...)`.

items.title: feat(parsers): support YAML MCP / OpenAI tool manifests (`*.yaml`, `*.yml`)
items.summary: Load tool definitions from YAML manifests when `PyYAML` is installed (gracefully skipping when absent).
items.motivation: Agent frameworks (CrewAI, AutoGen, declarative MCP gateways) frequently store tool schemas in `.yaml` files.
acceptance_criteria: Use `yaml.safe_load` when `pyyaml` is available; never use unsafe `yaml.load`.
Reuse `_normalize_tool_entry` from `json_manifest.py` to avoid code duplication.
Add unit tests for YAML tool manifests and non-tool YAML configs (e.g., GitHub Actions workflows must be ignored cleanly).

items.title: feat(parsers): intra-module helper function taint propagation for security rules (MCP005-MCP007)
items.summary: Follow 1-hop calls from `@mcp.tool()` functions to module-local helper functions (`_run_cmd(...)`, `_fetch(...)`) when extracting `CodeSink` entries.
items.motivation: Production MCP servers often delegate execution to private helper functions in the same file. Propagating tainted parameter flow across 1-hop helper calls significantly increases security recall.
acceptance_criteria: Index top-level helper functions in the same AST module and detect sinks reachable when a tool passes a parameter into a helper call.
Avoid infinite recursion on mutually recursive helpers.
Add unit tests verifying sinks inside `_helper(url)` are attributed to the calling `@mcp.tool()`.

items.title: feat(rules): add MCP012 live protocol and transport validation
items.summary: Validate a running server's handshake and tools/list response: unsupported protocol revision, missing `tools` capability, malformed entries, pagination.
items.motivation: The original item reserved MCP009 for this, but MCP009 ended up as hardcoded secrets and protocol validation shipped as the live-only MCP012. Rule IDs are a public contract, so the manifest follows the code rather than the reverse.
acceptance_criteria: Use a non-conflicting rule ID and document supported protocol assumptions.
Test supported and unsupported transport configurations without executing a server.

items.title: feat(engine): deterministic per-finding risk scoring and `risk_index`
items.summary: Add configurable risk scoring using finding severity, exploitability and available mitigations.
items.motivation: A documented score can help operators prioritize findings consistently.
acceptance_criteria: Define and document deterministic scoring weights and output fields.
Test score boundaries, mitigated findings and compatibility with existing reports.

items.title: feat(cli): baseline comparison so CI gates only new findings
items.summary: Compare current and previous scan results to identify new, resolved and unchanged findings.
items.motivation: Scan comparisons make regressions and remediation progress visible.
acceptance_criteria: Specify stable diagnostic matching keys and an explicit comparison interface.
Test added, resolved and unchanged findings, including malformed baseline input.

items.title: feat(cli): add `vexar-mcp simulate` model cost projection
items.summary: Project catalog token cost into per-call and monthly spend for a chosen model, built on the same estimator that drives MCP002/MCP014.
items.motivation: Operators need transparent estimates of tool-schema context costs.
acceptance_criteria: Load tool schemas from the requested input rather than a placeholder example.
Document pricing units and assumptions; test model selection and unknown-model behavior.

items.title: feat(policies): `strict-prod` and `enterprise-governance` presets
items.summary: Provide documented strict-production and enterprise-governance policy presets.
items.motivation: Reusable policy settings reduce inconsistent deployment checks.
acceptance_criteria: Define supported preset settings and explicit override precedence.
Test preset loading, invalid names and backward compatibility with existing configuration.

items.title: feat(dashboard): published report feed with score trend
items.summary: Expose audit-report JSON data and historical trends in the dashboard.
items.motivation: Teams need a readable view of audit results and changes over time.
acceptance_criteria: Specify a versioned report feed and history format.
Test missing reports, escaped untrusted display content and trend calculations.

items.title: feat(plugin): declarative rule packs for custom and community rules
items.summary: Design explicit opt-in discovery and configuration of third-party rule packs.
items.motivation: Organizations need extensible checks without implicitly trusting or running arbitrary plugins.
acceptance_criteria: Document the plugin trust boundary and require explicit opt-in.
Reject duplicate rule IDs and test disabled plugins and load errors.

items.title: chore(release): prove PyPI trusted publishing end to end
items.summary: The publish workflow now builds, verifies and uploads via OIDC (pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish). What remains is the PyPI-side trusted publisher registration and one real publish to confirm the round trip.
items.motivation: It shipped broken: the workflow requested id-token: write and then ran `twine upload`, which cannot use an OIDC token, with no token supplied. It is fixed, but 'the workflow exists' is not 'publishing works' — that needs a real release to prove.
acceptance_criteria: Trusted publisher is registered on PyPI for this repo, workflow and environment.
A patch release publishes automatically from a GitHub Release with no secret.
`pip install vexar-mcp==<version>` in a clean environment yields a working `vexar-mcp`.
The version in pyproject.toml, the tag, the release and PyPI all agree.

items.title: feat(cli): enumerate and audit multiple MCP servers from a registry file
items.summary: Add `vexar-mcp audit-registry <file>` that reads a list of server commands (or a Claude/Cursor MCP config), audits each one with the live stdio client, and emits a single combined report.
items.motivation: Teams run several MCP servers, often defined in one client config. Auditing them one command at a time is the difference between a tool used daily and a tool used once.
acceptance_criteria: A registry file schema is documented and validated with fail-closed errors.
Each server is audited in isolation; one server failing to start does not abort the run and is reported as exit-worthy.
Reports aggregate per-server scores plus a fleet-level summary, in terminal/JSON/HTML.
Fixture-based tests cover a broken server, a clean server, and a partially failing fleet.

items.title: feat(policies): support organization and team policy inheritance
items.summary: Allow a policy file to extend a built-in preset and layer team overrides, with deterministic precedence and an auditable resolution chain.
items.motivation: Enterprises need one org standard with narrow, reviewable team exceptions. Today that means copy-pasted TOML that silently drifts.
acceptance_criteria: Policies can declare `extends = "strict-prod"` plus explicit overrides.
Protected categories cannot be re-enabled for ignoring by a child policy.
`--print-config` shows the full resolution chain and which file contributed each setting.
Deterministic precedence is covered by tests, including conflicting layers.

items.title: feat(policies): enforce server-wide token budget as its own gate
items.summary: Turn `max-server-tokens` into an enforced finding instead of a reported configuration value, so a server cannot silently exceed its aggregate context budget.
items.motivation: Per-tool budgets are enforced; the aggregate budget that actually drives per-turn cost is not. Teams hit the aggregate limit first.
acceptance_criteria: A rule (new ID, documented) fires when total estimated tokens exceed `max-server-tokens`.
Presets set the budget consistently with their per-tool values.
The finding appears in terminal/JSON/SARIF output and can be baselined.
Tests cover just-under, exactly-at, and over-budget servers.

items.title: feat(loaders): optional tree-sitter backend for TypeScript tool registration
items.summary: Add an opt-in parser backend that resolves computed tool names, imported schema factories and referenced handlers, while keeping the dependency-free lexical loader as the default.
items.motivation: The lexical loader is honest about its limits but cannot follow real SDK usage: `server.tool(TOOL_NAME, DESC, createSchema(), handler)` registers an invisible tool. A coverage contract is documented; a stronger backend closes the gap.
acceptance_criteria: Backend selection is explicit (`--ts-parser lexical|tree-sitter`) and documented, with lexical remaining the default.
Installing the optional extra does not change behaviour unless selected.
Fixture coverage shows which constructs each backend recognises and which remain invisible.
The JSON report records which backend ran, so coverage is comparable across runs.

items.title: feat(loader-contract): per-file tool-completeness signals
items.summary: Detect constructs the loader saw but could not resolve (computed registration names, imported schemas) and report them as analysis issues, so partially-understood files lower status instead of silently passing.
items.motivation: Today a file with computed tool registration parses cleanly and reports `clean`. That is the same false-confidence shape as the fail-open parse bug, one level deeper.
acceptance_criteria: A new issue kind (`unresolved_tool`) is emitted with file, line and construct description.
It lowers status to `partial` without being counted as a security finding.
False-positive rate on the fixture corpus is documented before enabling by default.

items.title: test(benchmarks): reproducible token-estimator accuracy benchmark
items.summary: Replace the empirical ~8% claim in tokens.py with a committed benchmark against real tokenizers over representative MCP schemas, and document the method.
items.motivation: The estimator drives MCP002 and MCP014, so its accuracy is a product claim. Claims in docstrings that are not reproducible should not exist.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark corpus is committed with provenance and licensing.
Reported error distribution (mean, p95, worst case) is generated by a script, not asserted by hand.
The docstring cites the measurement and the script that produces it.
An optional exact-tokenizer extra is documented as opt-in only.

items.title: chore(pricing): make the simulate price table reviewable and self-checking
items.summary: Add a dated, machine-checked pricing manifest so `vexar-mcp simulate` cannot quietly quote a stale rate.
items.motivation: Prices live in a Python dict with an `as_of` string that nothing verifies. A cost projection that silently ages is the same false-confidence failure the scanner was rebuilt to remove.
acceptance_criteria: The table moves to a data file with a `reviewed_on` date per entry.
A test fails when any entry is older than a configured review window.
`simulate` warns in output when the table is past its review window.

items.title: docs(usage): walk through policy + baseline in a CI job
items.summary: Add a copy-pasteable section to docs/usage.md showing a full GitHub Actions job that scans with `--policy ci`, adopts a baseline on the first run, and gates only new findings.
items.motivation: The two most common support questions are 'how do I turn this on without failing on day one?' and 'why did my score change?'. Both are answered by one worked example, which is cheaper to write than to keep answering.
acceptance_criteria: The example runs as written against `examples/` in a fresh checkout.
It shows both the adopting run (`--write-baseline`) and the enforcing run (`--baseline`).
Every command in the snippet is checked by a test or CI step, or is marked as illustrative.
It states what happens on the second run when nothing changed.

items.title: feat(live): audit remote servers over Streamable HTTP
items.summary: Add an HTTP transport for `audit-server` so remote MCP deployments can be audited, with the origin, header, caching and auth checks the specification requires.
items.motivation: The audit path is stdio-only, which covers local servers and nothing else. The 2026-07-28 revision defines `MCP-Protocol-Version` routing headers, origin validation rules and cache scoping that a stdio-only client never has to think about.
acceptance_criteria: HTTPS only; plaintext HTTP refused unless explicitly allowed for loopback.
`MCP-Protocol-Version` sent and validated against the response.
`Origin` validated and reported as an MCP012 finding when missing or foreign.
Response bodies, redirects, and total duration bounded; no private-range requests unless opted in.
Private security results are never treated as publicly cacheable.
Two negotiation modes (handshake and stateless) work over HTTP as they do over stdio.

items.title: fix(engine): refuse to read files whose realpath leaves the scan root
items.summary: Skip, or gate behind `--follow-symlinks`, any scanned file that resolves outside the requested target, and report the skip as a coverage note.
items.motivation: Review finding F-05: a symlinked file inside a scanned tree is read even when it points at `/etc/passwd`. Content is never echoed, so the impact is small — but least privilege says a scanner should read what it was pointed at and nothing else, and it should say when it declines to read something.
acceptance_criteria: A file whose resolved path is outside the target root is skipped by default and counted in coverage as skipped.
`--follow-symlinks` restores today's behaviour for monorepos that rely on it.
The skip is visible in terminal output, not silent: a scanner must not quietly read less.
Tests cover: symlinked file inside the tree, symlink escaping it, symlinked directory (already not followed), and a broken symlink.

items.title: docs(spec): keep a per-revision compatibility matrix current
items.summary: Move the compliance matrix out of the review document into `docs/compliance.md`, and add a test that fails when a new MCP revision exists that Vexar-MCP does not support.
items.motivation: F-01 happened because a protocol revision shipped and nothing in the repository noticed. A review document is a snapshot; this needs to be a standing artefact with a check attached.
acceptance_criteria: `docs/compliance.md` lists each supported revision with its negotiation mode and the fixture that proves it.
A test asserts every revision in `SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` has a fixture exercising it.
The README links the matrix next to the live-audit docs.

items.title: chore(ci): unify GitHub Action pins so one major runs per action
items.summary: The repository pins actions/checkout at v4, v5 and v7, and actions/github-script at v7 and v9. Different majors of the same action mean two workflows can behave differently for no visible reason, and it is how the setup-python drift in PR #61 happened: one Dependabot PR was closed unmerged and four files were bumped by hand, leaving five on the old major.
items.motivation: Actions drift silently. checkout v7 blocks checking out fork pull requests under pull_request_target, and welcome-bot.yml combines pull_request_target with checkout@v4 -- so this cannot be a blind bump, which is exactly why it needs to be a reviewed task rather than a Dependabot merge.
acceptance_criteria: Every workflow and action.yml uses one major per action.
Welcome-bot is resolved deliberately: either it keeps an older checkout pin with a comment explaining why, or it stops checking out under pull_request_target.
The pin-drift ratchet in tests/test_docs_and_assets.py drops its allowlist, so the test is what enforces it from then on.
